properties.title: Cardiac Copilot: Automatic Probe Guidance for Echocardiography with World Model

membership.reason: Implements Cardiac Dreamer, a transformer-based latent transition world model predicting adjacent cardiac plane features from 6-DoF probe motion, coupled to a guidance policy G.
membership.counting_boundary: Implemented core latent-transition world model (WT_ACQUISITION) with formal capability downgraded to unknown (offline single-step pose-guidance MAE evaluated only; no future-state rollout or closed-loop control evaluation).

properties.backbone: ResNet-34 encoder E + Transformer Cardiac Dreamer I(f_{t1}, a_{t1->t2}) + 3-layer FC guidance policy G

properties.flow: 2D echo image S_t -> ResNet-34 encoder -> Cardiac Dreamer latent transition -> Guidance layer G -> 6-DoF probe guidance command (59.4 ms inference)

properties.purpose: Real-time 6-DoF probe guidance for freehand echocardiography (PLAX, PSAX-AV, PSAX-MV).
properties.environment: Offline held-out volunteer scans (15 scans, 37K samples)

criteria_met: Offline 6-DoF probe-guidance pose MAE and AE standard deviation evaluated on 15 unseen-individual test scans (37K images) across PLAX, PSAX-AV, and PSAX-MV, reducing MAE by 2.9%–33.1% vs policy-only baseline (Table 1, Fig. 3).
criteria_missing: Closed-loop navigation task success rate, multi-step control/trajectory execution, or prospective decision endpoint (Section 4 defers autonomous robotic scanning to future work).

assertions.rationale: Single-image inference time measured at 59.4 ms on RTX 3090.
Transition operates in ResNet-34 feature space.

evidence_fragments.content: The core innovation lies in proposing a data-driven world model, named Cardiac Dreamer, for representing cardiac spatial structures. This world model can provide structure features of any cardiac planes around the current probe position in the latent space, serving as an precise navigation map for autonomous plane localization. We train our model with real-world ultrasound data and corresponding probe motion from 110 routine clinical scans with 151K sample pairs by three certified sonographers. Evaluations on three standard planes with 37K sample pairs demonstrate that the world model can reduce navigation errors by up to 33% and exhibit more stable performance.

The ultrasound image data was acquired from health adult male volunteers using a Franka Panda robot arm with an ultrasound probe (M5S probe, GE Vivid E7 machine) manipulated by professional echocardiographers, meanwhile the pose information of the probe was also recorded synchronously by utilizing Robot Operation System (ROS). Overall, approximately 188K cardiac ultrasoundimages pairedwithprobemotionwere collectedfrom125routine clinical scans, forming a diverse dataset for training the proposed Cardiac Copilot models. The whole data collecting process was approved and supervised by The Tsinghua University Science and Technology Ethics Committe. Data processing involved aligning relative pose coordinates of each image with target planes which were identified by professionals, ensuring a unified coordinate system for each plane. The dataset was split into 110 scans (about 151K images) for training and 15 scans (about 37K images) for testing. Note that the test set included individuals not seen during training to evaluate the algorithm’s generalization.

As shown in Fig. 2, the model architecture includes a ResNet-34 for feature extraction, a guidance layer with three fully connected layers (the output dimensions are 2048, 512, and 6), and a Cardiac Dreamer network based on the original transformer architecture proposed in [18]. Additionally, one-hot encoding for plane selection is introduced, allowing the model to adapt relative pose predictions based on the chosen target plane. Model training, conducted with Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) training on four NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs, spanned 300 epochs. The training process employed the CosineAnnealingLR scheduler with 0.0001 learning rate, AdamW optimizer, and Automatic Mixed Precision (AMP). For inference, we tested on an Nvidia RTX 3090, and the inference time for a single image is 59.4ms which meets practical requirements.

capability_assessments.rationale: Downgraded honestly from L4 to unknown: Cardiac Dreamer implements a learned action-conditioned latent transition I(f_{t1}, a_hat_{t1->t2}) -> f'_{t2} coupled to an imitation-learning probe-guidance network G, but reported evaluation (Table 1, Fig. 3) measures only offline single-step 6-DoF pose-regression MAE (up to 33.1% reduction vs baseline) without future-state rollout fidelity (no L1/L2), without matched alternative-action successor comparisons (no L3), without closed-loop control/navigation task success (L4 do_not_assign_when excludes action-label/pose prediction alone), and without standalone representation-quality probing/reconstruction evaluation (L0 not used as fallback).

limitations: Evaluated offline on healthy adult male volunteer scans; no prospective closed-loop sonographer or patient trial.
Single-step target-oriented lookahead rather than multi-step trajectory planning.

Evaluates only offline single-step 6-DoF pose-imitation MAE (no future-state prediction fidelity evaluation, no matched alternative-action successor comparison, and no closed-loop control/navigation task success), leaving formal L0-L4 capability level unestablished (unknown).

legacy_cells.B: Cardiac Copilot: Automatic Probe Guidance for Echocardiography with World Model
legacy_cells.C: Jiang, Haojun, Sun, Zhenguo, Jia, Ning, Li, Meng, Sun, Yu, Luo, Shaqi, et al.
legacy_cells.S: Can a learned model use the current echocardiographic view and relative plane position to improve guidance toward a standard cardiac plane?
legacy_cells.T: Healthy adult male volunteers undergoing routine cardiac ultrasound scans; test data included individuals unseen during training.
legacy_cells.V: Choose a six-dimensional probe movement guidance signal toward a selected standard echocardiographic plane.
legacy_cells.AI: Ultrasound images; relative six-dimensional probe position/motion
legacy_cells.AJ: ResNet-34 image feature encoder; Cardiac Dreamer based on the original Transformer architecture; three-layer fully connected guidance layer
legacy_cells.BD: Six dimensions: translation in x, y, z and rotation in roll, pitch, yaw.
legacy_cells.BI: Cardiac Copilot system; Cardiac Dreamer world model
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted latent feature of a corresponding cardiac plane from the current image feature and relative positional relationship.
legacy_cells.BT: Guidance layer predicts six-dimensional probe movement toward the selected target plane.
legacy_cells.DQ: 125 routine clinical scans; approximately 188K image–probe-motion pairs (110 scans/about 151K training; 15 scans/about 37K testing).
legacy_cells.EC: Probe-guidance pose MAE improved across all six components on three planes; largest reported reductions: 27.5% (PLAX z translation), 26.3% (PSAX-AV rz rotation), and 33.1% (PSAX-MV ry rotation).
legacy_cells.EG: Single-image inference time: 59.4 ms on an NVIDIA RTX 3090.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared Cardiac Dreamer with a baseline comprising the feature encoder and guidance layer; Cardiac Dreamer reduced pose MAE across translation and rotation components on all three planes.
legacy_cells.ER: Data collection was approved and supervised by the Tsinghua University Science and Technology Ethics Committee.
legacy_cells.FB: Current ultrasound image is encoded into a learned feature vector; Cardiac Dreamer predicts a feature for another cardiac plane conditioned on relative probe/plane position.
legacy_cells.FL: ResNet-34 encodes the current ultrasound image into a feature; Cardiac Dreamer maps that feature plus relative plane pose to a predicted adjacent-plane feature; the guidance layer predicts target-plane probe motion; an action-combining operator composes guidance signals. No closed-loop robot execution is reported.
legacy_cells.FM: The authors introduce Cardiac Dreamer, a learned latent map of cardiac plane structure conditioned on relative position, and integrate it with an imitation-learning probe-guidance network.
legacy_cells.FN: On three standard planes, Cardiac Dreamer reduced pose-guidance MAE versus the baseline across all translation and rotation components; the largest reported reductions were 27.5%, 26.3%, and 33.1%.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors identify directing a robotic arm for fully autonomous cardiac ultrasound scanning as future work.
legacy_cells.FQ: The introduction states that publicly available research on cardiac probe navigation was lacking and describes limitations of prior guidance in degrees of freedom and generalizability.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is an offline held-out evaluation on scans from the collected cohort. The paper does not demonstrate prospective clinical benefit, reader assessment, external/multisite validation, causal treatment effects, or closed-loop autonomous robot scanning; autonomy is described as future work.
